commits.edited_message:
[gpu] Share the work budget through the public draw API

hb_gpu_paint reached into the scratch encoder by writing its
external_budget pointer directly, so a whole paint session could share
one work counter.  Drive that sharing through the public draw-budget API
instead: seed the scratch encoder with hb_draw_set_budget() before each
clip glyph (and before a client-drawn clip path) and read the remainder
back with hb_draw_get_budget_remaining(), so the COLR walk aggregates its
work without touching encoder internals.  The transforming pen now exposes
the scratch encoder's own live counter rather than the paint session's.

Give linear and sweep gradients the same three-texel parameter header as
radial gradients.  The additional texel is zero-filled and ignored by the
current shaders, making the three payload layouts uniform.

Tests: meson test -C build (275/275 passed); the CFF/COLR gpu-fuzzer
regression seed completes in 0.46s.

Assisted-by: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>

[gpu] Fix 32-bit overflow in hb_gpu_paint_encode() and cap sub-blob bytes

hb_gpu_paint_encode accumulated the lengths of all sub-blobs into a
32-bit unsigned without an overflow check, then allocated the output
from the wrapped total.  A COLRv1 paint DAG that revisits a max-size
gradient enough times could therefore make the buffer tiny while the
copy loop wrote the real data, overflowing the heap.

Maintain the running sub-blob byte total while each blob is pushed and
allocate from that checked total instead of summing the vector again.
Gradient pushes account for their parameter header and color stops as
they are emitted, and all sub-blob pushes fail once the total exceeds
64 MiB.

Tests: meson test -C build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <claude-sonnet-5.5@anthropic.com>

coupling: The first edited commit safely normalizes linear and sweep gradient sub-blobs to the same three-texel parameter header used by radial gradients. At that point allocation remains exact because encode still sums each blob's real length. The later edited commit replaces that exact sum with a running total maintained while pushing gradient blobs. Its accounting formula uses the older two-texel header size for linear and sweep gradients, which is exact on the original parent but undercounts each such blob by eight bytes after the earlier header normalization. hb_gpu_paint_encode() then allocates from the undercounted total while the final copy loop uses each blob's real length, producing a heap-buffer-overflow. The two edits must be reconciled across the header-layout change and the later size-accounting consumer; examining either maintenance change in its original context does not reveal the stale cross-commit size assumption.
